A FL on Weekly will contain at least 2 or 3 FLs on 4hr. It will contain many more on a 1 minute chart. However, only a few of those 1 or 5 min FLs would be near the HTF boundary, have fresh orders, proper LS, etc. It is our job to identify which one(s) to trade after we get an engulf. The following user(s) said Thank You: Ywicked , jigga , zee , Al3cs , GGJJ , Frosty , Nytewyre , Balzak , Astrokillah , einrikr , reaq Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You My attempt to show AK how I think about scales 06 Oct 2017 10:59 #143 Rinehart Topic Author --> Away Associate Trader Posts: 450 Thank you received: 927 I used Weekly, 4hr and 15 min charts to breakdown important areas. If I wanted to go to even smaller time frames, I would probably use 4hr, 15 min and 1 min. I'm sure it is possible to go from Monthly to 1min. But your charts would be unreadable. I haven't talked about Eng in these charts because I wanted to impress on you the importance of playing "important FLs." The ones around the boundaries. It is our job to find the good ones. We also of course need PA to tell us where ITs want to go. Now to think a little bit about Eng. If we have an Eng of of a 1 min FL without engulfing any HTF FLs. Well, that is PA and we can expect price to reach the next 1 min FL before breaking the FL behind us. You can play it and place targets based on the 1 min chart. On the other hand, if you have an engulf on daily chart, then you can use daily targets. Now think about the video IF made showing GBPUSD Daily. The QM video where he showed a 50R trade. This was a LS kink QM trade. Now imagine that you dropped from daily down to 15 min to sharpen your SL. It is as simple as that. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. The trade is still viable but late in the day on Friday is dangerous. Liquidity Providers widen spreads to stop out suckers. My observation is that normally they widen the ASK line (on top) and leave the bid line. Above the ask is where my SL resides so I'll avoid the danger. Why the ask line? Because our charts are setup to print candles from the Bid prices. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Some personal incite 21 Feb 2018 02:25 #222 Rinehart Topic Author --> Away Associate Trader Posts: 450 Thank you received: 927 Considering Frosty's recent journal posts as well as some PMs from newer members asking for advice about learning RTM and trading in general, I'd like to give a little perspective: Learning the materials taught at RTM does not mean you have to trade the way IF trades. In trading the only thing that truly counts is having a positive equity curve! IF is able to nail near zero drawdown, high R trades. That is something to strive for but it is not the main goal. I think some members get so caught up trying to learn how to nail perfect RTM trades, they lose sight of the most important goal. Your purpose with RTM has to be to find a way to read the market better. Armed with a better understanding of where price wants to go and where it will not violate, you can find ways to trade that match your personality and situation. AK is a 1 min scalper. I trade larger time frames mostly set and forget due to work. This works fine for both of us. On the other hand, I am not a scalper and AK isn't comfortable with set and forget. The fact is both of us have incorporated RTM into what works for us and we use it to grow our equity. Could AK learn to set and forget or could I learn to be a scalper? Possibly, but we don't have to. We have found something that works for us. We can stay in our lane, rinse and repeat. With RTM, you don't need to learn how to nail a 5 pip SL 150 R/R trade. You achieve your goals by growing your equity curve. Case in point, here is a trade I took on Gold today. My entry was absolutely not a RTM entry. This is not a trade I would normally post on RTM because it doesn't fit with the way members are taught to trade. We are taught to sell at supply yet this was a breakout trade. I took the trade because I knew where price wanted to go. RTM gave me knowledge of the engulf and I used that knowledge to trade what was given. FOCUS ON GROWING YOUR EQUITY, PERIOD. Take from RTM what you need to become profitable, period. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. I haven't talked about Eng in these charts because I wanted to impress on you the importance of playing "important FLs." The ones around the boundaries. It is our job to find the good ones. We also of course need PA to tell us where ITs want to go. Now to think a little bit about Eng. If we have an Eng of of a 1 min FL without engulfing any HTF FLs. Well, that is PA and we can expect price to reach the next 1 min FL before breaking the FL behind us. You can play it and place targets based on the 1 min chart. On the other hand, if you have an engulf on daily chart, then you can use daily targets. Now think about the video IF made showing GBPUSD Daily. The QM video where he showed a 50R trade. This was a LS kink QM trade. Now imagine that you dropped from daily down to 15 min to sharpen your SL. It is as simple as that. In trading the only thing that truly counts is having a positive equity curve! IF is HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT able to nail near zero drawdown, high R trades. That is something to strive for but it is not the main goal. I think some members get so caught up trying to learn how to nail perfect RTM trades, they lose sight of the most important goal. Your purpose with RTM has to be to find a way to read the market better. Armed with a better understanding of where price wants to go and where it will not violate, you can find ways to trade that match your personality and situation. AK is a 1 min scalper. I trade larger time frames mostly set and forget due to work. This works fine for both of us. On the other hand, I am not a scalper and AK isn't comfortable with set and forget. The fact is both of us have incorporated RTM into what works for us and we use it to grow our equity. Could AK learn to set and forget or could I learn to be a scalper? Possibly, but we don't have to. We have found something that works for us. We can stay in our lane, rinse and repeat. With RTM, you don't need to learn how to nail a 5 pip SL 150 R/R trade. You achieve your goals by growing your equity curve. Case in point, here is a trade I took on Gold today. My entry was absolutely not a RTM entry. This is not a trade I would normally post on RTM because it doesn't fit with the way members are taught to trade. We are taught to sell at supply yet this was a breakout trade. I took the trade because I knew where price wanted to go. RTM gave me knowledge of the engulf and I used that knowledge to trade what was given. FOCUS ON GROWING YOUR EQUITY, PERIOD. However, only a few of those 1 or 5 min FLs would be near the HTF boundary, have fresh orders, proper LS, etc. It is our job to identify which one(s) to trade after we get an engulf. If I wanted to go to even smaller time frames, I would probably use 4hr, 15 min and 1 min. I'm sure it is possible to go from Monthly to 1min. But your charts would be unreadable. I haven't talked about Eng in these charts because I wanted to impress on you the importance of playing "important FLs." The ones around the boundaries. It is our job to find the good ones. We also of course need PA to tell us where ITs want to go. Now to think a little bit about Eng. If we have an Eng of of a 1 min FL without engulfing any HTF FLs. Well, that is PA and we can expect price to reach the next 1 min FL before breaking the FL behind us. You can play it and place targets based on the 1 min chart. On the other hand, if you have an engulf on daily chart, then you can use daily targets. Now think about the video IF made showing GBPUSD Daily. The QM video where he showed a 50R trade. This was a LS kink QM trade. Now imagine that you dropped from daily down to 15 min to sharpen your SL. It is as simple as that. Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Report to moderator Quick Reply Reply Quote Thank You Some personal incite 21 Feb 2018 02:25 #222 Rinehart Topic Author --> Away Associate Trader Posts: 450 Thank you received: 927 Considering Frosty's recent journal posts as well as some PMs from newer members asking for advice about learning RTM and trading in general, I'd like to give a little perspective: Learning the materials taught at RTM does not mean you have to trade the way IF trades. In trading the only thing that truly counts is having a positive equity curve! IF is able to nail near zero drawdown, high R trades. That is something to strive for but it is not the main goal. I think some members get so caught up trying to learn how to nail perfect RTM trades, they lose sight of the most important goal. Your purpose with RTM has to be to find a way to read the market better. Armed with a better understanding of where price wants to go and where it will not violate, you can find ways to trade that match your personality and situation. AK is a 1 min scalper. I trade larger time frames mostly set and forget due to work. This works fine for both of us. On the other hand, I am not a scalper and AK isn't comfortable with set and forget. The fact is both of us have incorporated RTM into what works for us and we use it to grow our equity. Could AK learn to set and forget or could I learn to be a scalper? Possibly, but we don't have to. We have found something that works for us. We can stay in our lane, rinse and repeat. With RTM, you don't need to learn how to nail a 5 pip SL 150 R/R trade. You achieve your goals by growing your equity curve. Case in point, here is a trade I took on Gold today. My entry was absolutely not a RTM entry. This is not a trade I would normally post on RTM because it doesn't fit with the way members are taught to trade. We are taught to sell at supply yet this was a breakout trade. I took the trade because I knew where price wanted to go. RTM gave me knowledge of the engulf and I used that knowledge to trade what was given. FOCUS ON GROWING YOUR EQUITY, PERIOD. Take from RTM what you need to become profitable, period. Attachments: Check this box to be notified of replies to this topic. Note: BBcode and smileys are still usable. QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Some personal incite #222 Rinehart Offline Associate Trader Posts: 453 Thank you received: 1016 Considering Frosty's recent journal posts as well as some PMs from newer members asking for advice about learning RTM and trading in general, I'd like to give a little perspective: Learning the materials taught at RTM does not mean you have to trade the way IF 29/37 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2884-rinehart-s-journal?start=200 7/27/2018 Rinehart's Journal - Page 9 - RTM Community trades. In trading the only thing that truly counts is having a positive equity curve! IF is HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT able to nail near zero drawdown, high R trades. That is something to strive for but it is not the main goal. I think some members get so caught up trying to learn how to nail perfect RTM trades, they lose sight of the most important goal. Your purpose with RTM has to be to find a way to read the market better. Armed with a better understanding of where price wants to go and where it will not violate, you can find ways to trade that match your personality and situation. AK is a 1 min scalper. I trade larger time frames mostly set and forget due to work. This works fine for both of us. On the other hand, I am not a scalper and AK isn't comfortable with set and forget. The fact is both of us have incorporated RTM into what works for us and we use it to grow our equity. Could AK learn to set and forget or could I learn to be a scalper? Possibly, but we don't have to. We have found something that works for us. We can stay in our lane, rinse and repeat. With RTM, you don't need to learn how to nail a 5 pip SL 150 R/R trade. You achieve your goals by growing your equity curve. Case in point, here is a trade I took on Gold today. My entry was absolutely not a RTM entry. This is not a trade I would normally post on RTM because it doesn't fit with the way members are taught to trade. We are taught to sell at supply yet this was a breakout trade. I took the trade because I knew where price wanted to go. RTM gave me knowledge of the engulf and I used that knowledge to trade what was given. FOCUS ON GROWING YOUR EQUITY, PERIOD. Take from RTM what you need to become profitable, period. https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2884-rinehart-s-journal?start=200 30/37 7/27/2018 Rinehart's Journal - Page 9 - RTM Community HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Attachments: 31/37 https://www.readthemarket.com/index.php/en/forum/journals/2884-rinehart-s-journal?start=200 7/27/2018 Rinehart's Journal - Page 9 - RTM Community The following user(s) said Thank You: hansma, lv5758, Ywicked, alirezat, GGJJ, Frosty, HOME EDUCATION FORUM MORE LOGOUT Balzak, Astrokillah, dengaima, Enkim, haanz, Gero, peter941221, Captain Caveman QUICK REPLY REPLY QUOTE THANK YOU Some personal incite #223 Astrokillah Offline Associate Trader I don't quit Posts: 488 Thank you received: 762 Ryan, well said, well said,... now if I can learn how to set and forget like you..
